The working file is the complete analysis; the Markdown/PDF reports are reader copies of it. Each should be read in full — this message is not the analysis.

Bottom line (MEDIUM confidence): the correct ceiling is the ideal reversible-component, best-known-architecture Rankine-cycle efficiency for a 565°C source and 30–45°C sink — approximately 47–54% (central ~51%) — not naive Carnot (62–64%, an unachievable abstraction for a sensible-heat-source steam cycle) and not Curzon-Ahlborn (38–40%, a mischaracterized efficiency-at-maximum-power result that current practice already exceeds). Current practice sits at ~42% gross (NREL/TP-5500-57625, read at source), roughly 9 percentage points below that ceiling — about half the ~20-point gap naive Carnot would suggest. Of those 9 points, roughly 4–5 are recoverable with known, demonstrated technology (supercritical pressure, double reheat, better HX and turbine design), though much of that is currently uneconomical at CSP's unit scale, and roughly 4–5 are structurally or economically locked in by CSP-specific constraints (turbine scale penalty, dry-cooling siting, salt return-temperature floor). The dominant source of uncertainty is an estimate-based ground truth (GT-11?, the Carnot-fraction bracket used to derive the ~51% central ceiling); a direct steam-table ideal-cycle calculation is the single most useful follow-up to tighten this analysis.
